title: Bespoke small-prime AVX2 kernel for GF(251) charpoly+minpoly residual cells
description:
Close the two residual GF(251) cells left open after the d1dd266c+sibling integration — both share the small-prime AVX2 kernel-call-overhead root cause and need bespoke register-scheduled kernels in `gf2-kernels-simd`. Tracked here under 615db3b9's broader finite-field LA catch-up umbrella.

## Cells to close

| Cell | Pre-integration | Post-integration | 1.5x ceiling | Gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GF(251)/n=64 minpoly | 4.04x | 2.84x | 0.202 ms | 1.9x past ceiling |
| GF(251)/n=256 charpoly | 9.58x | 3.18x | 1.975 ms | 2.1x past ceiling |

Evidence: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` §§ 6.1, 6.2.

## Background

Sibling tasks `5a3dbd5b` (canonical-byte chain_polys) and `70766cb1` (panel-kernel inline + Barrett-table cache) closed the algorithmic and dispatch overhead. The residual gap is now the per-call AVX2 byte-lane operation cost:

- **GF(251)/n=64 minpoly:** 4 panel iterations × ~50 ns/iteration AVX2 lane/register setup. fflas hand-tunes a small-n register-scheduled kernel.
- **GF(251)/n=256 charpoly:** chain_polys `sub_scaled_into` per-call function-pointer indirection + Barrett-constant load. fflas fuses the chain_polys update with the matvec inner loop.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Both target cells PASS the 1.5x ceiling vs fflas-ffpack on Zen 3 with reproducible measurements.
- [hard] Implementation respects unsafe-isolation: any new register-scheduled kernels live in `gf2-kernels-simd`; the safe `gf2-core` API surface stays unchanged.
- [hard] No regression on any cell currently PASSing in `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` §§ 3.1–3.2.
- [hard] Correctness: bit-identical scalar-equivalence proptests for the new kernels at boundary lengths {0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65, 255, 256}.
- [hard] Final evidence updates `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` (or successor) with the closed cells.

## Notes

This task is a follow-up to `d1dd266c` + siblings — it does NOT block their closure. The `97bf0879` epic accepts the partial 14/16 result via the user-approved 2026-05-07 amendment routing the residual constant-factor closure to this follow-up. Filed as a `615db3b9` dependency to attach it to the broader finite-field LA SOTA catch-up plan.
